advances: A single positive convex fiber and the actual exterior traces of its complete geometric active cells. The identity is on positive rates.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Write $\ell_j=(-\log L_j)_+$. The volume interiors of distinct full-dimensional active cells are disjoint, and their union covers volume almost everywhere. Their exterior traces from the interior partition the original boundary up to surface-null sets. On a tie plane coinciding with a body facet the interior-side cell supplies the trace. An internal interface where exactly two full-dimensional cells are incident is counted with opposite outward normals. Multiple tie planes meeting in codimension at least two have zero interface area. If several ties coincide in one hyperplane, the affine slopes transverse to that plane order their values on each side, so only the two interior traces there count.

Consider an interface between different groups. If $c_i,c_k$ are nonparallel, the gradient of $A_{ij}$ along $\{A_{ij}=A_{kj}\}$ has norm $\lVert c_{ij}\wedge c_{kj}\rVert/\lVert c_{ij}-c_{kj}\rVert$, bounded below for large $j$. Linear coarea in that hyperplane and the common outer ball bound give
$$
\int_{\text{interface}\,\cap\,\{A_{ij}<\varepsilon\}}\ell_j\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}
\le C\int_0^\varepsilon(-\log s)\,ds \qquad(0<\varepsilon<1).
$$
The transverse sections have uniformly bounded $(d-2)$-volume, including counting in $d=2$. If the limiting gradients are parallel, a sequence of common interface values tending to zero would give a point in $K$ on both limiting zero sets. A positive constant plane cannot vanish, and for nonzero parallel gradients this makes the zero hyperplanes equal and the two affine functions positively proportional by their values at $o$. The parallel case therefore has a uniform positive floor. These estimates give uniformly small logarithmic tails on every intergroup interface.

For integer $m\ge1$, apply Gauss–Green to $\phi\ell_j r_j^m$ on the cells in $G$, where $\phi$ is a smooth physical scalar test. This function is continuous at all interfaces, so those within $G$ cancel exactly. On an intergroup interface the integral of $\ell_j r_j^m$ tends to zero: use the uniform tail bound and compact rate bound on the large-log part, and $r_j\to0$ uniformly on the bounded-log part. The same argument uses bulk uniform integrability for the term with $\nabla\phi$. On cell $i$ the derivative of $\ell_jr_j^m$ is $-(m+1)r_j^m c_{ij}/A_{ij}$ almost everywhere, including the zero-rate region. Taking the joint limits yields
$$
-\int\phi n R^m\,d\beta_G=M(m+1)\sum_{i\in G} c_i\int\phi s^m\,d\zeta_i.
$$
All positive-rate limiting positions have $L=0$ and those belonging to cell $i$ have $A_i=0$ by coefficient convergence. Every limiting exterior normal is a genuine support normal, and $h$ is bounded below by a fixed inradius at $o$. Testing the vector identity with $\phi(X)(X-o)$ gives radial moments since $c_i\cdot(X-o)=-b_i$ on the inverse defect. The uniform probability $U_R$ has moment $R^m/(m+1)$. Finite measures on the compact rate range with equal positive-degree moments against every spatial test agree on the positive rates. Indeed, continuous functions vanishing at zero are uniformly approximated by polynomials vanishing there, and finite sums of separated continuous spatial and rate tests determine the joint law. Both measures give zero mass to rate zero, so this proves the radial identity.

For the normal, the restriction of $A_{ij}$ to the rectifiable boundary has tangential gradient $c_{ij}-(c_{ij}\cdot n)n$. On the region where its norm is at least $a>0$, boundary coarea bounds its logarithmic mass in $\{A_{ij}<\varepsilon\}$ by $(C/a)\int_0^\varepsilon(-\log s)\,ds$. For almost every intermediate level the boundary section is the relative boundary of the convex $(d-1)$-section, whose perimeter in the section plane is uniformly bounded in the common outer ball. For example, partition its boundary by a coordinate in which the unit normal has magnitude at least $1/\sqrt{d-1}$ and its sign, and use the area formula on the corresponding upper or lower convex graph. In $d=2$ the section perimeter counts at most two endpoints. The same tail bound applies on the active exterior trace, where $A_{ij}=L_j$. Since $A_{ij}\le e^{-r_0/\lambda_j}$ for rates $\ge r_0>0$ on that trace, every positive-rate normal in its limit is parallel to $c_i$. A zero gradient gives a strictly positive constant plane and no such defect. The possible normal $+c_i/\lVert c_i\rVert$ has negative dot product $-b_i/\lVert c_i\rVert$ with $X-o$ on the zero plane, contradicting the fixed inball. The other normal yields $h=b_i/\lVert c_i\rVert$, independent of $i$ in the group. Divide the radial identity by this common positive constant. Groups with no exterior defect have no inverse defect by the positive radial weights, so the second identity holds for them as well.
statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let convex bodies $K_j\subset\mathbb R^d$ converge in Hausdorff distance to a convex body $K$, and let $L_j=\min_i A_{ij}>0$ on $K_j$ for a fixed finite family of affine functions converging coefficientwise to $A_i$, with $L=\min_i A_i>0$ on $\operatorname{int}K$. Take $M_j\to M>0$ and $\lambda_j>0$ with $\lambda_j\to0$. Suppose the inverse masses $\int_{K_j}(M_jL_j)^{-1}\,dX$ and exterior positive-log masses are bounded, the bulk logarithms are uniformly integrable, and $r_j=\lambda_j(-\log L_j)_+$ lies in a fixed compact interval. Form the actual active cells $C_{ij}=K_j\cap\{A_{ij}=\min_l A_{lj}\}$, merging identical planes and discarding volume-null cells, and select a subsequence with fixed surviving indices and simultaneous joint limits. Let $\zeta_i$ be the positive-rate part of the joint limit of $\mathbf1_{C_{ij}}\,dX\,\delta_{r_j}/(M_j L_j)$. Group the retained indices by positive proportionality of the limiting affine functions.

For a group $G$ let $\beta_G$ be the positive-rate part of the joint limit of $(-\log L_j)_+\,dS_j\,\delta_{r_j}$ on the actual exterior traces of its cells, where $dS_j$ records physical position and the outward unit normal. Fix $o\in\operatorname{int}K$, put $b_i=A_i(o)$, $h=n\cdot(X-o)$ and $B_G=\pi_*(h\beta_G)$, where $\pi$ forgets the normal only. Write $U_R$ for the uniform probability on $[0,R]$. Then
$$
M\sum_{i\in G} b_i\zeta_i(dX,ds)=\int_{R>0} U_R(ds)\,B_G(dX,dR).
$$
If the group's exterior defect is nonzero, its planes have nonzero gradients $c_i$, and $\beta_G$ is carried by $n=-c_i/\lVert c_i\rVert$, the same normal for all $i\in G$. On it $h=b_i/\lVert c_i\rVert$ is constant. In particular, for the projected exterior defect $\mu_G=\pi_*\beta_G$,
$$
M\sum_{i\in G}\lVert c_i\rVert\zeta_i(dX,ds)=\int_{R>0} U_R(ds)\,\mu_G(dX,dR).
$$
title: Separate positive-rate kernels and exterior normals for actual affine groups
